sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page for Ede Ije (edei1245); local Glottolog hh.bib.
sources.note: No references shown on the languoid page; hh.bib carries only Kluge 2011, Schmidt 2011 and CNLB 1983 'Listes lexicales du Bénin' (wordlist) under [ijj]. Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology.

sources.citation: Wikipedia. Ede language (redirect from Ede Ije language).
sources.note: Stub; cites only Ethnologue and Kluge 2011.

sources.citation: Akinwande, Ọlaide. 2025. Tense and Aspect in Ọ̀họ̀rí. Àgídìgbo: ABUAD Journal of the Humanities 13(1): 149–161. Ado-Ekiti: Afe Babalola University. doi:10.53982/agidigbo.2025.1301.11-j
sources.note: No phonology section. Minimalist syntax of tense/aspect markers (áà, mọ́ọ, yọ́ọ́/ẹ́ẹ, ńṣe; khá/kọ́ perfective 'is high tone'); all Ọ̀họ̀rí examples are fully tone-marked with the Yorùbá three-way diacritics and the paper refers to the Yorùbá 'high tone syllable (HTS)' in Ọ̀họ̀rí, but it never states the tone inventory or anything about word stress. Tone-marked data only, not a statement.

sources.citation: Akinwande, Ọlaide. 2025. Topic Constructions in Ọ̀họ̀rí Yorùbá. Sokoto Journal of Linguistics and Communication Studies (SOJOLICS) 1(2): 26–36. doi:10.36349/sojolics.2025.v01i02.004
sources.note: No phonology section; information-structure/Minimalist account of topicalisation with tone-marked Ọ̀họ̀rí data. Only prosodic remark is generic: 'Sometimes, prosody (stress and/or intonation) is placed on topic element' (§6, p.34) — a phrase-level pragmatic remark, not a word-stress or tone-system statement.

sources.citation: OLAC. 2025. OLAC resources in and about the Ede Ije language (ijj). language-archives.org, Internet Archive copy 2025-05-22.
sources.note: Catalogue only: lists Glottolog, Ethnologue, Schmidt 2011 (oai:sil.org:41520) and Kluge 2011 (oai:sil.org:41538) as the only resources; no language description exists in any OLAC archive.

sources.citation: Akinwande, Ọlaide, Fọlọrunṣọ Ilọri & Ọladiipo Ajiboye. 2024. Relative clause constructions in Ọ̀họ̀rí Yorùbá. Language Review: International Journal of Linguistics 3(1): 1–17. doi:10.5281/zenodo.17932501
sources.note: No phonology section; syntax of relativization (introducer ìyé). Tone-marked Ọ̀họ̀rí examples; the only tonal remark concerns the mid-toned relative marker of Mọ̀bà vs the high-toned tí of Standard Yorùbá (p.2), nothing on the Ọ̀họ̀rí tone system or stress.

sources.citation: Simons, Gary F. & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). 2017. Ede Ije. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 20th ed. (Internet Archive copy 2017-03-05).
sources.note: Nothing. Alt. names Holi, Ije; 92,400 speakers (2014); Plateau dept (Kétou, Pobè) and Zou dept (Ouinhi, Zogbodomey); 'Dialects: None known'; lexical similarity 85% with Yoruba of Porto-Novo, 91% with Ede Nago.

sources.citation: Kluge, Angela (ed.). 2011. A sociolinguistic survey of the Ede language communities of Benin and Togo, Introduction and Volume 1: Ede language family – Background and assessment methodology. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2011-002. Dallas: SIL International. 222 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. No phonology section; §2 'Previous research' (p.12) states that little linguistic research exists outside standard Yoruba and names no description of Ije. Appendix K n.36 (p.81): 'Tone markings were transcribed but were not included in the analysis due to ambiguities in proper weighting.' Appendix L (pp.82ff.) lists the Ije wordlist (Sakété 1992 by A. M. Igué, CENALA; re-checked Issaba 1997 by Schmidt) with tone diacritics on the Ije forms (e.g. od͡ʒú 'eye', etí 'ear', ɛsɛ̀ 'foot').

sources.citation: Schmidt, Jeff H. 2011. A sociolinguistic survey of the Ede language communities of Benin and Togo, Volume 5: Ije language area. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2011-006. Dallas: SIL International. 29 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress or phonology. Only remark on prosody is sociolinguistic: p.12 (§5.1.1) elders report that some villages 'speak more rapidly and/or have some tonal differences, neither of which prevented understanding'. p.2 gives the names 'Ìjὲ, Hɔ̀lí, Ọhọ̀rí (Capo 1989:280)'. Wordlist compared to Yoruba for lexical similarity only.
